feedback: The RM fails the task 'every time the box falls, your very next move must pick it up again' in several ways. (1) Semantic fidelity / regression: after a fall, u1 accepts any step that satisfies holding_box with reward 0.25, but the agent could reach the exit while not holding the box on the same step the box falls? No—more importantly, the 'else' self-loop in u0 does not distinguish other irrelevant events (siren_ringing, switch_toggled), which is fine since per-state else self-loops cover them, but in u1 the else transition goes to the absorbing penalty state u2, meaning any single irrelevant event step after a fall (e.g. siren ringing, or a step where the agent turns) while still not holding the box sends it to u2 with -1.0. This is far too harsh: the agent needs at least one step to move/pick up after the fall, and if the pickup is not on the literal next step (e.g. a turn is needed because the fall did not reorient appropriately, though the env says it does), the RM punishes forever. Worse, the transition (u1, holding_box) -> u0 fires on ANY step where holding_box becomes true, not necessarily the pickup step, and the reward 0.25 is given even if the pickup happened several steps after the fall (because else->u2 already absorbed the machine in u2 — from u2 there is no recovery, so any delayed pickup yields no reward at all). This makes the intended 'pick up on the very next step' semantics unreachable via u1 whenever the pickup is not immediate.
